I added open and close transitions to all three. The changes are only in `src/styles.css`; `app.js` still toggles `hidden` and `.is-open` as before. I haven't checked any of this in a browser.

**How it works:** Each element now uses CSS transitions instead of switching instantly. Because these are transitions, a quick second click (opening the menu again while it's closing, or saving again while the toast is fading) reverses smoothly from wherever it is instead of jumping. `@starting-style` provides the starting point for the open animation, and `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` keeps the element visible until the close animation finishes.

- **Opening:** fade in over `--duration-medium` (250ms) using `--ease-standard`, the timing your tokens already define.
- **Closing:** shorter, a 150ms fade using `ease-out`.
- **Movement and blur** only run when the user hasn't turned on the system's reduced-motion setting. With it on, each element just fades.

**Per element:**
- **Account dropdown:** drops in from 12px above and lifts back up as it closes, with a slight blur.
- **"Changes saved" toast:** rises 12px into place and exits 12px upward. I kept your existing `-50%` horizontal centering in each position.
- **Delete-account modal:** the dark backdrop fades, and the card moves 12px into place with a blur. This replaces `transition: all 400ms ease`, which never animated anything: the modal switched straight from `display: none` to `display: flex`, so there was no visible starting state to animate from.

**Browser support:** this animation method works in Chrome 117+, Safari 17.4+ and Firefox 129+. In older browsers the elements still open and close, just without animation.

**Not part of this request, but worth knowing:**
- The modal doesn't move keyboard focus into itself or close on Escape.
- The menu's `:hover` style isn't limited to devices with a mouse, so on touch screens it can stay highlighted after a tap.

I can fix either of these if you'd like.

I added open and close transitions to the account dropdown, the "Changes saved" toast and the delete-account modal. I didn't run it in a browser, so I haven't seen or replayed any of the motion yet.

All the changes are CSS in `src/styles.css`. `src/app.js` didn't need any changes because it already shows and hides these three with the `hidden` attribute and the `is-open` class. The CSS keeps each element on screen while it fades out, so the close can animate too, not just the open.

**How they move:**
- **Opening:** 300ms. The element fades in, rises 12px and comes into focus from a 4px blur.
- **Closing:** 150ms (your existing `--duration-short` setting). It fades out, moves up 12px and blurs.
- **Interruptions:** if someone clicks again halfway through, the motion turns around smoothly instead of jumping. For example, they might close the menu before it finishes opening, or save again while the toast is fading out.
- **Reduced motion:** for people who have turned on "reduce motion" in their system settings, all three only fade, with no movement or blur.

**What changed in each one:**
- **Account dropdown:** fades and slides as above.
- **"Changes saved" toast:** same motion. I kept its existing horizontal centring, so it stays in the middle of the screen while it moves.
- **Delete-account modal:** this one had a 400ms fade that never actually played, because the modal went from completely hidden to visible in a single step. That's now fixed. The dark background fades in and out, and the card moves.

**Browser support:** this uses fairly new CSS features: Chrome/Edge 117+, Safari 17.4+, Firefox 129+. Older browsers still show and hide all three correctly, just with no animation.

**Not fixed:** the hover highlight on the dropdown items (line 19) isn't limited to devices with a mouse. On touch screens it can stay highlighted after a tap. It's a separate fix, and I can do it if you'd like.

I added open and close transitions for all three in `src/styles.css`. The JS didn't need any changes: `app.js` already toggles `hidden` or `.is-open`, and the CSS now animates those changes. I haven't run it in a browser, so none of this has been checked visually.

**Why the modal didn't animate:** `.modal` switched straight from `display: none` to `display: flex`. Since `display` can't be animated, the browser skipped the fade, and the `transition: all 400ms ease` never ran.

**The fix, used for all three:** `@starting-style` gives each element a style to animate in from. `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` keeps it on screen until its close animation ends. Each one names the properties it animates instead of using `all`. Opening reverses smoothly if someone clicks again halfway through.

| Element | Open | Close |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account dropdown | Fades in and drops 4px into place, 250ms | Fades out and rises 4px, 150ms |
| "Changes saved" toast | Fades in and rises 12px with a light blur clearing, 300ms | Fades out, moving 12px up with a light blur, 150ms |
| Delete-account modal | Backdrop fades in; the card rises 12px and the blur clears, 300ms | Backdrop fades out; the card lifts 12px and blurs, 150ms |

The dropdown uses the project's existing timing and easing tokens (`--duration-medium`, `--ease-standard`). I gave it a smaller 4px movement because 12px would be more than the 8px gap between the button and the menu. Closing is shorter than opening on all three.

**Reduced motion:** the movement and blur only run for users who haven't turned on the reduced-motion setting. Everyone else gets a plain fade rather than an instant pop.

**Browser support:** `@starting-style` and animating `display` work in all current major browsers. Browsers older than 2024 will still show and hide these instantly, as they do now.

**Separate issue, not changed:** the modal doesn't move focus into the dialog and doesn't close when you press Escape. That's an accessibility fix rather than an animation one, so I left it alone.

I added open and close transitions for all three in `src/styles.css`. I didn't need to change any JavaScript, because the existing code that shows and hides them now triggers the animations. I haven't checked this in a browser.

**How they move**
- **Account dropdown:** fades in and grows from 0.96 to full size, starting from its top-right corner because that's where it's attached under the button.
- **"Changes saved" toast:** fades in while sliding up 12px, and reverses on the way out.
- **Delete-account modal:** the dark backdrop fades in and the card grows from 0.96 to full size. Before, it popped in and out because it was shown and hidden instantly, which skipped its 400ms transition. It now animates both ways.

**Timing**
- Opening takes 250ms and closing takes 150ms, so things leave faster than they arrive. Opening uses the project's existing `--duration-medium` and `--ease-standard` settings from `tokens.css`, and closing uses `--duration-short`.
- If someone reopens or closes an element mid-animation, it reverses smoothly from where it is instead of jumping.
- If a user's system is set to reduce motion, all three only fade, with no sliding or scaling.

**Browser support:** this uses fairly new CSS features (`@starting-style` and animating `display`), supported in browsers since 2024. Older browsers will show and hide instantly, as they do now, so nothing breaks.

**Accessibility issues I noticed but didn't change:**
- The delete modal can't be closed with Escape and doesn't keep keyboard focus inside it. Switching it to a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()` would fix both.
- The dropdown items' hover style isn't limited to devices with a mouse, so on touchscreens it can stay highlighted after a tap.

**What was wrong**
- **Dropdown and toast:** both switch `display: none` on and off through the `hidden` attribute. An element has no earlier style to transition from at that point, so they just appeared and disappeared.
- **Modal:** it had `transition: all 400ms ease` on an element that switches between `display: none` and `flex`. The fade never ran, and `all` transitions every property that changes.

**What I changed**
- **Shared setup** (`styles.css:51-77`):
  - The transitions now cover only opacity, scale, translate and display.
  - `@starting-style` gives each element a starting state when it opens.
  - `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` keeps each one visible until its close animation ends.
  - Opening takes `--duration-medium` (250ms) and closing takes `--duration-short` (150ms), both with `--ease-standard`. These come from your existing `tokens.css`.
  - The motion reverses smoothly if someone toggles mid-animation.
- **Dropdown:** fades and grows from 0.96 scale out of its top-right corner, where the button is, and shrinks back there on close.
- **Toast:** slides up from below the bottom of the screen while fading in, and drops back down on dismiss.
- **Modal:** the dark background fades, and the card scales from 0.96 out of its centre.
- **Reduced motion:** the scaling and sliding only run when the user hasn't asked for reduced motion. Otherwise all three just fade.

**Browser support:** this relies on `@starting-style` and transitioning `display`. Recent versions of all major browsers support both. Older browsers fall back to showing and hiding instantly, which is how it worked before.

**Accessibility issues I noticed but didn't fix:**
- The toast is a status message (`role="status"`) that starts out hidden. Screen readers may not announce "Changes saved" when it appears. Keeping the element on the page and only changing its text is more reliable.
- The modal doesn't move keyboard focus into itself or close on Escape.
- The dropdown's hover highlight isn't limited to devices that can hover, so on touch screens it can stay lit after a tap.

Two newer CSS features make that animatable: `@starting-style` gives the element a starting point to animate from when it appears, and `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` keeps it on screen until the close animation finishes. Opening takes 250ms and closing 150ms, using the timing and easing values already in `tokens.css`. If a user clicks again mid-animation, it reverses smoothly from where it is.

| Element | Opening | Closing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account dropdown | Fades in and grows from 96% to full size, starting at its top-right corner (the corner under the button) | Fades and shrinks back toward that corner |
| "Changes saved" toast | Fades in and rises 16px from the bottom of the screen | Fades and drops back toward the bottom |

**Files changed**
- `src/styles.css`: the transitions for the menu, toast and modal. I also removed the modal's old `transition: all 400ms`, which never animated because the modal jumped straight from hidden to shown.
- `index.html`: the modal starts with the `hidden` attribute.
- `src/app.js`: the modal opens and closes by setting `modal.hidden` instead of adding and removing the `is-open` class.

**Browser support:** this works in Chrome 117+, Safari 17.4+ and Firefox 129+. Older browsers still show and hide everything correctly, just with no animation.

**Problems I noticed but didn't fix:**
- The modal doesn't behave like a real dialog yet. Focus doesn't move into it or stay inside it, and Escape doesn't close it. Switching it to a `<dialog>` element opened with `showModal()` would fix all of that, and the same transitions would carry over to its built-in `::backdrop`.
- The **Delete** button inside the modal doesn't do anything when clicked.
- The `.menu a:hover` style isn't limited to devices with a mouse (`@media (hover: hover)`), so on touch screens a tapped menu item can stay highlighted.

All three now animate open and closed. The changes are CSS only, in `src/styles.css`. `app.js` still toggles `hidden` and `.is-open` the same way, and the CSS animates those changes.

**What each one does**

**Browser support:** this relies on newer CSS features (`@starting-style` and animating to and from `display: none`), which all major browsers have supported since 2024. Older browsers will show and hide the elements instantly, as they do today.

- The menu's hover background isn't limited to devices with a mouse, so on touchscreens it can stay highlighted after a tap.
- The modal doesn't move keyboard focus into itself, keep focus inside while open, or close on Escape. Switching it to a native `<dialog>` would handle these.
